newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $0.50 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $0.50 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices early Monday were steady to $0.50 per cwt higher amid light marketings, livestock dealers and packer buyers said.

Hot, humid weather over the weekend that sent heat index readings near 110 degrees Fahrenheit in parts of Iowa and 100 in Illinois, was seen persisting Monday, which could retstrict already thin marketings, they said.
Several southern Minnesota hog buyers said thunderstorms late Sunday cooled temperatures a bit, but farmers were still slow showing up at country buying stations and plants early Monday.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold steady to $0.50 per cwt higher at $57.50 to $58.50 in the country and $59.00 to $59.50 for hogs delivered to the plant, sources there said.

Illinois hogs sold steady to $0.50 higher at $58.00 to $59.00 in the country and $59.00 to $59.50 at plants. Several packers reportedly paid up to $60.50 for top quality hogs, dealers and packer buyers there said.
Indiana hogs sold $0.50 higher at $57.50 to $58.00 in the country and $59.50 to $60.00 at plants. Ohio hogs sold steady to up $0.50 at $55.50-$56.50/country and $57.50-$58.50/plants.
